name: Spirit Animals
tagline: Two confirmed, and both of them explain a name the Archive had already got wrong.
body:
A CATEGORY THE ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW IT HAD. Women in this family carry a spirit animal, and in at least two cases the animal is where the name came from — which means the Archive has been inventing etymologies for epithets whose real source was sitting one field away.

LUCIA WILDING — A LIONESS. She is a PLAYFUL TOP and her spirit animal is a lioness; stack those two facts and THE PLAYFUL LIONESS is finished without a single strand of hair in it. The Archive instead learned that her hair is burnt honey shot with crimson and unkempt as a mane, and reached BACKWARDS to rewrite an existing epithet as having been caused by it. A coincidence promoted to an etymology. The mane is real. It is not the reason.

ABIGAIL SILVERVEIL — A FOXHOUND. Which is where FOXXY comes from, her wife’s name for her, and which the Archive briefly took to be addressed to SELENE because Lumina had used a similar word in a corridor once. Selene is FOXMOM. Different office entirely.

THE RULE THIS GIVES THE SCRUB: WHEN A NAME HAS AN OBVIOUS DERIVATION, CHECK WHETHER SHE HAS AN ANIMAL FIRST.
rules: Lucia Wilding — lioness. Playful top plus lioness = The Playful Lioness
Abigail Silverveil — foxhound. Hence FOXXY, from Lumina
SELENE IS FOXMOM, to the whole family. Cora said it first and it stuck
Check for an animal before explaining an epithet
